# Clear responsibilities

| Package | Responsibility | Primary representations |
|---|---|---|
| SpaMTPData | Discoverable experiment resources | Cardinal, SpatialExperiment, auxiliary files; labelled historical archives |
| SpaMTPdb | Versioned annotation and pathway resources | Independent tables/lists with checksums and provenance |
| SpaMTP | Analysis, annotation, plotting and explicit conversion | Existing Bioconductor S4 containers and public accessors |

SpaMTP imports SpaMTPdb and suggests SpaMTPData. Both data packages expose
resource interfaces that can be used independently of SpaMTP and Seurat. The
examples require SpaMTPdb >= 0.99.4 and SpaMTPData >= 0.99.5.

Package, RaMP and experiment-data releases have separate versions.

## Installation and example scope

Use `BiocManager::install(c("SpaMTP", "SpaMTPdb", "SpaMTPData"))` for packages
available in your Bioconductor release. The maintained
[installation guide](https://github.com/SpaMTP-project/SpaMTP#installation)
documents review-stage source installation, download timeouts and Windows
requirements. `citation("SpaMTP")` supplies the package reference.

This guide combines measured mouse-brain MSI/RNA and a mouse-bladder MSI
panel with pinned RaMP annotation resources. Resources are downloaded on first
use unless a verified local or cached copy is available. All code runs during
the build.

```{r packages, message=FALSE}
library(SpaMTP)
stopifnot(requireNamespace("SpaMTPData", quietly = TRUE))
```

# Data to a native analysis container

## Native experiment structure

```{r native-data}
spe <- SpaMTPData::spaMTPData("mouse_brain_dhb_striatum", version = "1.1.0")
stopifnot(methods::is(spe, "SpatialExperiment"))
SummarizedExperiment::assayNames(spe)
dim(spe)
SingleCellExperiment::altExpNames(spe)
```

The complete archived striatal dataset retains all measured mass features and
locations. It was previously selected by MSI clusters from one brain section.
Paired RNA in `altExp(spe, "SPT")` shares location names with MSI; independent
measurements require alignment and mapping before pairing.

## Normalization and spatial display

`LogNormalize` adds `logcounts`; `npcs = 2` requests two principal components.
Figure 3.\@ref(fig:preprocess) displays the measured mass nearest m/z 400.14659,
a focal feature in the original mouse-brain tutorial. Its spatial distribution can be examined alongside the
archived anatomy and side labels in the [complete workflow](End_to_End_Workflow.html).
Assigning a metabolite identity requires additional chemical evidence.

```{r preprocess, fig.width=7, fig.height=5, message=FALSE, out.width="450px", fig.cap="Measured m/z 400.14659 across all archived mouse-brain striatal locations. Each point retains its original image coordinates, displayed in thousands of pixels with y increasing downwards; colour shows LogNormalize intensity. All locations come from one specimen; comparisons describe variation within that specimen."}
spe <- normalizeSMData(spe, "LogNormalize", verbose = FALSE)
spe <- runMetabolicPCA(spe, npcs = 2, slot = "logcounts")
mz <- SummarizedExperiment::rowData(spe)$mz
feature_index <- which.min(abs(mz - 400.14659))
brain_map <- plotSpatialFeature(spe, features = rownames(spe)[feature_index],
  assayName = "logcounts", labels = sprintf("m/z %.4f", mz[feature_index]),
  pointSize = 1.3, combine = FALSE)[[1]]
brain_map +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(labels = function(z) z / 1000, n.breaks = 3) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_reverse(labels = function(z) z / 1000, n.breaks = 3) +
  ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  ggplot2::guides(colour = ggplot2::guide_colourbar(title.position = "top")) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Image x (1000 pixels)", y = "Image y (1000 pixels)",
    colour = "Logcounts")
SingleCellExperiment::reducedDimNames(spe)
```

Retrieve the embedding with `SingleCellExperiment::reducedDim(spe, "pca")`.
`metadata(spe)$reduction_inputs$pca` records the expression layer and features
used for PCA.

# Database discovery without network access

Both registry accessors return the same packaged metadata without downloading
resources.

```{r database-registry}
registry <- SpaMTPdb::spaMTPdbResources(version = "3.0.7")
stopifnot(identical(registry, spaMTPDatabaseInfo(version = "3.0.7")))
registry[registry$resource %in% c("chem_props", "smiles_features", "pathway"),
  c("resource", "version", "r_data_class", "bytes", "md5")]
```

## Verified resource retrieval

`loadSpaMTPDatabase()` validates file size and checksum and retains provenance.
Use `offline = TRUE` to reuse verified local files or cached downloads.
Set `local_dir` to the directory containing the published RDS files when
staging resources on a shared system.

```{r production-resources, eval=TRUE}
database <- loadSpaMTPDatabase(
  c("chem_props", "pathway"), version = "3.0.7"
)
stopifnot(nrow(database$chem_props) == 289754L)
```

`attr(database$chem_props, "spamtp_database")` exposes the resource version,
source URL and expected checksum for recording alongside analysis results.

# Measured bladder ions and RaMP candidates

The bundled bladder subset retains the spatial extent and all 79 features of
an archived annotated panel. Select its two ions nearest m/z 741.53058 and
798.54114 for a concise annotation example, retaining every supplied location.
Their historical labels are stored separately in `archived_lipid_candidates`.

`buildMZAnnotationIndex()` indexes the verified RaMP `chem_props` table using
potassium adducts (`M+K`, positive mode). `annotateSM()` searches within 5 ppm;
`min_score = 0` retains matched candidates for review. The database's
precomputed structure features are reused automatically.

```{r annotation}
bladder <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "bladder_demo.rds", package = "SpaMTP"))
bladder_mz <- SummarizedExperiment::rowData(bladder)$mz
ion_rows <- vapply(c(741.5305786, 798.5411377),
  function(target) which.min(abs(bladder_mz - target)), integer(1))
ions <- bladder[ion_rows, ]
index <- buildMZAnnotationIndex(database$chem_props,
  adducts = "M+K", polarity = "positive")
annotated <- annotateSM(ions, index = index, adducts = "M+K",
  polarity = "positive", ppm_error = 5, min_score = 0,
  return.only.annotated = FALSE, save.intermediate = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
stopifnot(identical(dim(annotated), dim(ions)))

candidates <- S4Vectors::metadata(annotated)$mz_annotation$results
candidate_counts <- tabulate(candidates$ID, nbins = nrow(annotated))
data.frame(
  measured_mz = SummarizedExperiment::rowData(annotated)$mz,
  archived_candidates = SummarizedExperiment::rowData(annotated)$archived_lipid_candidates,
  RaMP_candidate_records = candidate_counts)
annotationInfo(annotated)
```

## Candidate interpretation

The archived alternatives are SM 34:1 / PA 37:1 and PC 34:1 / PE 37:1;
SM, PA, PC and PE denote sphingomyelin, phosphatidic acid, phosphatidylcholine
and phosphatidylethanolamine. These labels preserve the archive's candidate
assignments. Each ion matches multiple RaMP records under the stated adduct
and mass tolerance; individual records can group several isomers. Resolving
these lipid identities requires additional chemical evidence. Scores use a
heuristic scale. The [annotation tutorial](Metabolite_Annotation_Pipeline.html)
covers index reuse and contextual scoring.

# Published native datasets and historical archives

The default resource release, `1.1.0`, provides seven native SpatialExperiment
datasets with URLs and hashes in
[Zenodo record 22733262](https://zenodo.org/records/22733262).
Historical Seurat files remain explicitly available in release `1.0.0`.

`metadata = TRUE` returns registry records without downloading data.
`native_metadata` describes release 1.1.0; `archive` describes the same
resource's historical 1.0.0 Seurat file.

```{r inspect-native}
native_metadata <- SpaMTPData::spaMTPData("mouse_brain_fmp10", metadata = TRUE)
stopifnot(native_metadata$version == "1.1.0",
  native_metadata$r_data_class == "SpatialExperiment",
  !native_metadata$requires_conversion)
```

```{r inspect-archive}
archive <- SpaMTPData::spaMTPData("mouse_brain_fmp10",
  version = "1.0.0", metadata = TRUE)
archive[, c("resource", "version", "r_data_class", "requires_conversion")]
stopifnot(identical(intersect(c("Seurat", "SeuratObject"), loadedNamespaces()),
  seuratBefore))
```

## Direct native-data retrieval

SpaMTPData's preparation recipe produces one native RDS per historical archive.
Retrieve these published files directly, without Seurat conversion.

`native` reuses the DHB/Visium object loaded above, with paired RNA in `SPT`.
`version = "1.1.0"` pins the data release independently of the package version.

```{r read-published-native, eval=TRUE}
native <- spe
SingleCellExperiment::altExpNames(native) # SPT
stopifnot(identical(colnames(SingleCellExperiment::altExp(native, "SPT")),
  colnames(native)),
  identical(intersect(c("Seurat", "SeuratObject"), loadedNamespaces()), seuratBefore))
```

Native files have separate checksums and provenance; original archives remain
unchanged. Counts and complete `data` layers are preserved without relabelling
`data` as `logcounts`. Optical rasters, polygons and Seurat graphs, weights and
reductions are omitted. Historical annotations, including `db_3`, retain their
original candidate assignments and provenance.

## Explicit archive conversion

Only this archive conversion requires SeuratObject. `legacy` is the historical
FMP10 object: `assay = "Spatial"` selects MSI and `image = "fov"` selects
coordinates. `converted_archive` has 1,538 features and 3,005 locations.

```{r convert-archive, eval=TRUE}
stopifnot(requireNamespace("SeuratObject", quietly = TRUE))
legacy <- SpaMTPData::spaMTPData("mouse_brain_fmp10",
  version = "1.0.0")
converted_archive <- seuratToSpatialExperiment(legacy, assay = "Spatial", image = "fov")
stopifnot(methods::is(converted_archive, "SpatialExperiment"),
  identical(dim(converted_archive), c(1538L, 3005L)))
```

Select coordinates, layers and images explicitly; optical rasters, graphs and
reductions are omitted. See [modern data access](Modern_Data_Access.html) for
conversion details and [the native workflow](SpaMTP_Bioconductor.html) for
analysis. The [migration table](Modern_Data_Access.html#migrating-existing-scripts)
lists common historical calls and their native replacements.
